assertions.description: The baseline: all five interfaces are defined on Window. If this fails the harness is wrong, not the browser.
The feature itself: the same five interfaces must be defined inside a dedicated worker, per [Exposed=(Window, Worker, ...)]. Before Chrome 154 every one of them was undefined there.
assertions.test: (async()=>{const src=`const n=['CSSStyleValue','CSSKeywordValue','CSSNumericValue','CSSUnitValue','CSSUnparsedValue'];postMessage(n.every((x)=>typeof self[x]==='function'));`;const url=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src],{type:'text/javascript'}));const w=new Worker(url);try{return await new Promise((res)=>{w.onmessage=(e)=>res(e.data===true);w.onerror=()=>res(false);setTimeout(()=>res(false),3000);});}finally{w.terminate();URL.revokeObjectURL(url);}})()

assertions.description: Being defined is not the same as being usable: the constructor must actually build a value with the right value and unit inside the worker.
assertions.test: (async()=>{const src=`try{const u=new self.CSSUnitValue(2.5,'rem');postMessage(u.value===2.5&&u.unit==='rem');}catch(e){postMessage(false);}`;const url=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src],{type:'text/javascript'}));const w=new Worker(url);try{return await new Promise((res)=>{w.onmessage=(e)=>res(e.data===true);w.onerror=()=>res(false);setTimeout(()=>res(false),3000);});}finally{w.terminate();URL.revokeObjectURL(url);}})()

assertions.description: Parsing is the operation that makes this worth having in a worker, and it must produce a CSSUnitValue rather than a string.
assertions.test: (async()=>{const src=`try{const v=self.CSSStyleValue.parse('width','16px');postMessage(v instanceof self.CSSUnitValue&&v.value===16&&v.unit==='px');}catch(e){postMessage(false);}`;const url=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src],{type:'text/javascript'}));const w=new Worker(url);try{return await new Promise((res)=>{w.onmessage=(e)=>res(e.data===true);w.onerror=()=>res(false);setTimeout(()=>res(false),3000);});}finally{w.terminate();URL.revokeObjectURL(url);}})()

assertions.description: CSSNumericValue.to() is the parser's own unit conversion, and it is the reason a token pipeline can move off the main thread without reimplementing arithmetic.
assertions.test: (async()=>{const src=`try{const v=self.CSSStyleValue.parse('width','2.54cm').to('mm');postMessage(Math.abs(v.value-25.4)<0.01&&v.unit==='mm');}catch(e){postMessage(false);}`;const url=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src],{type:'text/javascript'}));const w=new Worker(url);try{return await new Promise((res)=>{w.onmessage=(e)=>res(e.data===true);w.onerror=()=>res(false);setTimeout(()=>res(false),3000);});}finally{w.terminate();URL.revokeObjectURL(url);}})()

assertions.description: Module workers are Worker globals too, so the same exposure applies.
assertions.test: (async()=>{const src=`postMessage(typeof self.CSSUnitValue==='function');`;const url=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src],{type:'text/javascript'}));const w=new Worker(url,{type:'module'});try{return await new Promise((res)=>{w.onmessage=(e)=>res(e.data===true);w.onerror=()=>res(false);setTimeout(()=>res(false),3000);});}finally{w.terminate();URL.revokeObjectURL(url);}})()

assertions.description: The worker gets the real CSS parser, not a permissive one: a unitless number must be rejected for a length property. A regex fallback typically accepts it.
